data.narrative:
Fractile is a Series B semiconductor company that has raised $220M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors at similar or adjacent stages—including SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series A), Rebellions ($2.3B, Series A), d-Matrix ($2.0B, Series A), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C)—alongside 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $220M total raised as a proxy for base value, implying $418M. Peer-median anchoring across the 5-company private comparable set yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range from $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (20.5x median across public semis) cannot be applied due to the absence of Fractile's revenue disclosure, typical for private companies at this stage.

Triangulation of the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $355M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide range reflects material variance between stage-progression and peer-median approaches, and the substantial dispersion within the peer set itself—driven largely by SambaNova's outlier valuation. Key uncertainties include Fractile's revenue trajectory relative to peers and the appropriate stage-adjustment factor for Series B in this capital-intensive sector.
